title: Stochastic convex bandits: independent noise at two points and loss at the center.
summary: A fixed unknown convex Lipschitz objective is defined on a Euclidean ball. Each round permits two simultaneous probes, each returning an independently Gaussian-noised value. Only the center incurs the true objective loss; independent noise does not cancel in finite differences.

operations.query_signature: $$Y_t^+=f(z_t^+)+\varepsilon_t^+,\qquad Y_t^-=f(z_t^-)+\varepsilon_t^-,\qquad \varepsilon_t^\pm\overset{\mathrm{i.i.d.}}\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2).$$ The center $x_t$ and both probes $z_t^+,z_t^-$ must be submitted together before either observation is received. Noise is independent across all queries, with no shared seed. Only the center loss $f(x_t)$ is incurred; probe values are information queries and do not enter that round's loss. Causal policies may submit two simultaneous probes per round. Inputs $d,T,R,L,\sigma$ are public and $f$ is hidden. Both probes and the center must lie in the same ball. Past feedback may be stored and reused computationally; unrevealed past information and additional queries to exhausted samples are unavailable. Any within-round full-function or common-sample access must be explicit.

bounds.derivation: Contract the ball by proportion $a\in(0,1/2]$ and query the contracted center plus $aRu$, where $u$ is a random unit direction. The assumption $f(0)=0$ and Lipschitz continuity imply $|f(z)|\le LR$, and the gradient estimator has second moment at most $d^2(L^2R^2+\sigma^2)/(a^2R^2)$. Online gradient analysis gives $O(d\sqrt{L^2R^2+\sigma^2}\sqrt T/a+LRTa)$. Balance these terms and compare with the fixed-point strategy bound $2LRT$. Only one noisy value per round is needed; the second may be discarded. This argument does not use common-sample noise cancellation.
